name: email-send
description: Send a new email. Provide comma-separated recipient email addresses, subject, and body. Emails are sent from the agent's configured email address. Pass account to send from a named mailbox; when reply_to_message_id is set, the quoted original is read from that same mailbox.

inputs.subject: string
inputs.account: string? (named account to send from, as configured in channel_accounts.email. When reply_to_message_id is set, the original message is also read from this account. Defaults to the primary account.)
inputs.reply_to_message_id: string? (Nylas message ID — when set, the original message is quoted below the reply and the send is threaded)
inputs.attachments: object[]? (file attachments — array of {file_url: string, filename: string, content_type: string, node_id?: string}. file_url must be a file:// URL from email-download-attachment or similar. When the attachment contains KG-sourced data, set node_id to the kg_nodes UUID so export gates can resolve sensitivity. Max 10 attachments, 20 MB total.)
inputs.export_items: object[]? (parallel to attachments — array of {node_id: string, label: string} tagging each attachment's KG source for bulk-export gates. Required when sending confidential+ attachments; one entry per attachment in the same order.)
inputs.context_bridge: string? (JSON — optional context bridge registration that adds a delegation hint so the agent can route any reply faster. Tracking is automatic but best-effort even without it: registration happens after the send and can fail, and what it registers expires — unless you set expires_in_hours, about 3 days on email, the same with or without this parameter. A valid expires_in_hours replaces that default outright, in either direction: a smaller number gives a shorter window, not a longer one (a deployment may configure a different default). Set expires_in_hours whenever the reply may land after that — a request routed through an organisation's process rather than a person, an ask sent before a holiday or a long trip, anything a slow answer is normal for. If the entry expired or was never registered, the reply arrives as an unrecognised cold inbound. Shape: {agent_id, expected_reply?, delegation_hint?, metadata?, expires_in_hours?}. Example: {"agent_id":"coordinator","delegation_hint":"calendar-specialist","expected_reply":"confirmation or reschedule request"})
